name: VEXpath
one_liner: Hosted SBOM impact and VEX/CSAF workbench that tells mid-size product makers which CVEs actually affect each shipped release, priced for CRA compliance.

buyer.role: Head of product security / PSIRT lead (often the VP Engineering or quality/regulatory manager at smaller firms)
buyer.company_profile: EU-selling software vendors and connected-device / industrial equipment makers with 50-1,000 employees and 3-30 product lines; already generating SBOMs (Syft, CycloneDX plugins, Trivy) and often running self-hosted Dependency-Track, but with no answer for publishing VEX/CSAF advisories and documenting vulnerability handling before CRA reporting (since 11 Sep 2026) and main obligations (11 Dec 2027).

user: Product security engineers and release/firmware engineers who triage SBOM vulnerability findings per release, write 'not affected' justifications, and publish customer-facing advisories.

problem.summary: Mid-size manufacturers can now produce SBOMs, but cannot cheaply turn them into defensible answers to 'is our shipped release affected?'. Free Dependency-Track flags every CVE without parent-component, container or vendor-advisory context, cannot ingest vendor CSAF advisories, and treats BOM and VEX as separate uploads. Commercial platforms that do this are quote-only or $18k-$50k+ per year. Under the CRA, teams must handle vulnerabilities per product and report exploited ones within 24 hours, so noisy, unexplained findings become a compliance cost.

evidence.claim: Dependency-Track users ask for CSAF advisory ingestion because CPE is not granular enough to tell which part of a vendor product (e.g. RHEL) is affected.
Users ask to show the parent (root) dependency through which a vulnerable component is pulled in, so impact can be judged.
Teams analysing Trivy-Operator SBOMs in Dependency-Track cannot associate findings with the container they came from.
Some vulnerabilities only apply when a dependency is direct rather than transitive, so SBOMs need dependency hierarchy to judge exposure.
Dependency-Track manages BOM and VEX as separate entities, forcing a multi-step, wait-and-poll automation to keep them in sync.
Maintainers want a standard way to tell downstream users how an upstream advisory impacts their crate/binaries.
SBOM-based vulnerability management yields noisy results and VEX workflows to suppress false positives remain immature.
Commercial SBOM management with VEX is sold as annual contracts of $18,000 (10 active developers) to $100,000 (100).

why_now.summary: The EU Cyber Resilience Act's reporting obligations applied from 11 September 2026: manufacturers must send an early warning within 24 hours and a notification within 72 hours for actively exploited vulnerabilities, for all products on the EU market including those already sold. Its main obligations apply from 11 December 2027, leaving roughly a year to put vulnerability handling in place. Germany's BSI already publishes TR-03183 guidance, with a dedicated SBOM part (v2.1.0, with CycloneDX/SPDX field mapping) and a vulnerability reports part, aimed at manufacturers without mature security processes - exactly this buyer.

features.feature: Per-release SBOM ingest (CycloneDX/SPDX via CI action or API, plus import from an existing Dependency-Track instance) with full dependency-path view: root component, direct vs transitive, container/image of origin.
features.why: Gives the parent-component and container context users ask Dependency-Track for, and keeps teams' existing scanners and DT investment.

features.feature: Vendor CSAF advisory ingestion (Red Hat, Oracle, Siemens and other CSAF trusted providers) matched to SBOM components by PURL, overriding CPE-level false matches.
features.why: The most-engaged unmet request in the input; directly removes noise for device makers built on commercial distros.

features.feature: VEX triage workbench: queue of findings per release, status (affected / not_affected / fixed / under_investigation) with CISA-style justification picker, inherit-decision-across-releases, and reviewer sign-off.
features.why: Turns noisy findings into recorded decisions; reuse across releases is where small teams save time.

features.feature: Atomic publishing: export a release's SBOM plus matching CycloneDX VEX and CSAF 2.0 VEX/advisory documents, signed, to a hosted customer portal or the vendor's own site.
features.why: Solves the BOM/VEX sync problem and gives customers and authorities a machine-readable answer.

features.feature: CRA evidence pack: per product, a timestamped log of vulnerabilities, decisions and fix releases, plus a 24h/72h exploited-vulnerability draft triggered by a KEV listing.
features.why: Maps the work to the compliance deadline the buyer is paying to meet.

out_of_scope: SBOM generation and binary/firmware analysis (integrate Syft, Trivy, cdxgen; leave binaries to ONEKEY/Finite State)
Direct submission to the ENISA Single Reporting Platform (drafts only until its API is stable)
Licence compliance, full CRA conformity assessment and technical-file authoring

competitors.name: OWASP Dependency-Track (free, self-hosted)
competitors.how_we_differ: We import from it rather than replace it, and add what it lacks: vendor CSAF matching, parent/container context, atomic SBOM+VEX publishing, hosting and support.

competitors.name: sbomify
competitors.how_we_differ: sbomify is an SBOM publishing hub and trust center with a CRA wizard, scanning via OSV/Dependency-Track. We focus on the triage step before publishing: impact analysis, CSAF matching and VEX authoring. Likely partner or acquirer as much as rival.

competitors.name: Interlynk (SBOM Manager on AWS Marketplace)
competitors.how_we_differ: Interlynk prices by active developers from $18k/year. We price per product with public self-serve pricing well under that, for teams with few developers per product line.

competitors.name: Anchore Enterprise
competitors.how_we_differ: Anchore is a scanning and policy platform at $34.5k-$50k/year plus support. We don't scan; we sit on any scanner's output and specialise in VEX/CSAF and CRA evidence.

competitors.name: Manifest / Cybeats SBOM Studio / Finite State
competitors.how_we_differ: Quote-only enterprise platforms aimed at large medical and connected-device makers. We serve the mid-size tail they don't sell to, with self-serve onboarding.

competitors.name: Bundled cloud/registry SBOM features (AWS Inspector SBOM export, Docker Scout, GitHub attestations, JFrog Xray)
competitors.how_we_differ: They generate or attach SBOMs inside one platform. None produces cross-vendor, per-release VEX/CSAF decisions for customers and regulators.

differentiation: VEXpath is the only option priced and built for a mid-size manufacturer's real job: deciding, per shipped release, which CVEs matter and publishing that decision as VEX/CSAF. It keeps existing scanners and Dependency-Track, adds vendor-CSAF matching and dependency-path context to cut noise, and prices per product with self-serve onboarding, between free tools and $18k-$50k quote-led platforms.

build.team: 2 engineers (one with CycloneDX/CSAF standards experience) + 1 founder-seller with product-security/PSIRT background
hardest_parts: Reliable PURL matching between SBOM components and vendor CSAF product trees, which use inconsistent product identifiers
Carrying VEX decisions across releases safely: knowing when a dependency-path change invalidates an earlier 'not_affected'
Normalising messy real-world SBOMs (missing dependency graphs, mixed CycloneDX/SPDX versions, container layers)
Keeping pace with CRA harmonised standards and ENISA reporting-platform formats that are still being finalised

pricing.model: Annual SaaS subscription per product line (a product with its supported release branches), unlimited users; tiers by product count
pricing.entry_price: $490/month billed annually (~$5,900/year) for up to 5 products; $1,490/month for up to 25 products
pricing.rationale: Per-product pricing matches how CRA obligations attach (per product) and how mid-size makers think about cost, unlike per-developer pricing that punishes small firmware teams. The entry tier sits about 3x above sbomify Business, justified by triage and CSAF matching rather than publishing alone, and at roughly a third of Interlynk's smallest $18k contract, low enough for a team-lead card or a small purchase order without procurement.

comparables.price: $34,500 (Cloud Image) to $50,000 (Helm) per 12 months, plus $15,000 Essential support plan

go_to_market.first_customers: Ten EU (DACH/Nordics/Benelux first) industrial-automation, building-tech and IoT makers and B2B software vendors with 50-500 staff, already running Dependency-Track or Trivy, with a named person newly responsible for CRA, and with downstream OEM customers already requesting SBOM/VEX.
go_to_market.channel: Founder-led sales into the Dependency-Track and CycloneDX communities (an open-source CSAF-to-Dependency-Track bridge as lead magnet), CRA webinars with industry associations (e.g. ZVEI, VDMA) and partnerships with CRA consultancies and notified bodies who need a tool to recommend.
go_to_market.wedge: Free 'VEX in a day' import: connect an existing Dependency-Track instance, auto-resolve findings using vendor CSAF advisories, and show the noise cut (e.g. '412 findings to 37 that need a decision') before asking for payment.

risks: Crowding from below and above: sbomify already offers a CRA wizard and Dependency-Track scanning at $159/month, and funded vendors (Anchore, Interlynk, Manifest, ArmorCode) can add self-serve tiers as CRA demand grows.

Bundling: Dependency-Track may add CSAF ingestion and atomic BOM+VEX upload (both are open feature requests), and SCA suites or GitHub could ship VEX authoring, removing the core noise-reduction story.
Deadline-driven demand: many mid-size makers may defer spending until late 2027 or until a customer or market surveillance authority forces it, giving lumpy, late revenue.
Regulatory uncertainty: CRA harmonised standards and ENISA platform formats are not final; if they don't require VEX/CSAF specifically, the compliance hook weakens to 'nice to have'.
Technical: vendor CSAF coverage is uneven outside large vendors (Red Hat, Oracle, Siemens), so noise reduction may be much smaller for typical embedded stacks than the demo suggests.
Liability: customers relying on our 'not_affected' auto-suggestions in regulator-facing documents could blame us for wrong calls; decisions must stay human-signed.

riskiest_assumption.assumption: Mid-size EU manufacturers will pay ~$6k/year now (before December 2027) for VEX/CSAF triage on top of free Dependency-Track, rather than living with noise or buying a cheaper publishing tool like sbomify.
riskiest_assumption.test: Over 2 weeks, run 15 discovery calls with CRA owners at 50-500-person EU device/software makers sourced from Dependency-Track/CycloneDX community channels and an industry-association CRA webinar; show a clickable mock and one manual 'noise cut' on their own exported Dependency-Track findings, then ask for a paid pilot letter of intent at the entry price.
riskiest_assumption.success_signal: At least 4 of 15 sign a pilot LOI at $490/month or more, and at least 8 confirm an existing VEX/advisory request from a customer or a named budget for CRA tooling before end of 2027.

open_questions: Do CRA harmonised standards or market surveillance authorities expect VEX/CSAF specifically, or will any documented vulnerability handling do?
How much does vendor CSAF matching actually cut findings on typical embedded Linux / RTOS stacks versus enterprise distros?
Does sbomify (or another SBOM hub) already plan VEX authoring, making it a competitor rather than a partner?
Are Dependency-Track's CSAF (#2353) and atomic BOM+VEX (#1872) requests still open, and on its roadmap?
Who owns the budget in a 200-person device maker: product security, quality/regulatory or engineering?
Is per-product pricing understood by buyers, given how product lines and release branches vary?
